lines.text: The first crossbow bolt flew at Ash. It never reached him.
Wren's arrow hit it in mid-air, and split it in two.
What in the...
Shields! Now!
Thirty sellswords charged into the yard. Professionals. Men who had fought in three wars.
They had never fought Greyhollow.
Tobin caught a sword on the handle of his hammer, and the sword broke.
Old Hanne, who carried the water, swung a full bucket. A man in chainmail flew across the yard.
Wren fired from the roof of the mill. Three arrows, three sellswords down, and none of them dead. She aimed for the legs.
Ash didn't bite anyone. He didn't need to. He stood in front of the gate and roared, and the horses bolted with their riders still on them.
These aren't farmers! Nobody said they had knights!
And Bram. Bram walked through the middle of it all with his one arm and his old sword, and every man who stood in front of him ended up in the mud.
It was over before the sun had moved. Not one of ours had fallen.
Steward Corvin was still sitting on his horse, pale as milk.
Steward. You'll take your four thousand crowns, and your wounded, and you'll go home.
And you'll tell Lady Sabine the debt is paid. In full.
This isn't over, Varr.
It is for today.
They limped south down the muddy road. The villagers cheered until their voices gave out.
And I sat down very suddenly on the keep steps, because my legs had stopped working, and my hands were as cold as ice.
Nobody noticed. They were too busy celebrating.
Almost nobody.
Steward Bram. A word.
I have measured every person in this village. Thirty-seven commoners. Not one of them is below two rings. Three of them are at four.
That doesn't happen. Not in a lifetime. Not in a hundred lifetimes.
Do you know what he is?
Yes.
And he's not to know.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter nine, coming soon.
